The unsaved screen and session values as state machines (ADR-002 of Chapter 5.6), plus the task group tree (TaskGroup.treeState), the one saved value this file holds (SD-5 of table T-250). The keys are the state transition table keys of the NDD review standard, appendix A.6 'List of JSON Keys': `stateMachines[]`, one machine per orthogonal concern, each with `name`, `states` (state names, without `initial`), `transitions[]` and `unhandled[]`. Every key the project adds starts with `x`: per region (`xRegions[]`) the events it receives (defined once), the values its root carries and its guards; at the top `xGuardLanguage` and `xPriorities`; per machine its region (`xRegion`) and the facts of each state (`xStates`: the values it carries, its evidence, and an `entry` and an `exit` effect, run as UML runs them: exit, the transition's effect, entry; a transition to itself runs neither); per transition `xEffectArgument`, `xEvidence` and `xNote`. Inside the value of a project key the keys carry no `x`. What the manuscript holds and does not hold is table T-250 of docs/spec/05-07-design.md; the form of the machine is table T-249. state_machine_source.py is the one reader: it checks the shape the standard asks for and hands every generator the same region view.

NAMES, NOT NUMBERS (JDG-286, R4.4 of docs/development-rules/07-review-standards.md). A machine -- the definition -- is a noun phrase of what it tracks plus `StateMachine`, unique across every region (armModeStateMachine); the code holds its CURRENT state in a field and type named the same noun phrase plus `State` (armModeState, ArmModeState). A state reads 'the machine is now <state>': a past participle or adjective (taskShapeArmed, hidden, idle) or a present participle with its object (delivering, placingCursorA), never a bare noun; its id is machine.state (paletteDisplayStateMachine.shown.expanded). An event is subject plus past tense, defined once per region, id region/key (screen/armEntryPressed). A transition is named by its machine, source state and trigger.

A TRANSITION IS {source, target, trigger, guard?, effect?, xEffectArgument?, xEvidence, xNote?}; two or more with the same source and trigger are told apart by their guards. A transition from `initial` is the initial transition (source and target only): its target is the initial state at its level. A composite every transition enters by naming a child (armModeStateMachine.armed) has no initial child. The parent of a state is its name without the last word. EVERY PAIR OF A LEAF STATE AND AN EVENT THE MACHINE NAMES IS ANSWERED ONCE: by a transition from the leaf or from one of its composites (a transition on a composite answers for every state below it), or by an `unhandled[]` entry {source, trigger, handling} whose `handling` is `ignore` (the machine does not change and keeps the same reference, SD-3) or `error` (the pair must not occur). `target` equal to `source` is a transition to itself. A guard term is the name of a guard in the region's `guards` -- {name, condition, evidence, note?}, defined once per region, every one named by some transition or root cell -- or {in: <state id>} of ANOTHER machine of the region. `target` may be {name}: a value the event carries, standing for any top-level kind of the machine but its initial one; parent.{name} stands for any kind of that composite state but its initial one.

Generated FROM this file: _assets/tbl-state-machines.md (state_machines_json_to_md.py) -- per region the event definitions, the root's values and, per machine, its state diagram, its state transition table and its states; and, in the generated region of the unit each region names (`unit`; tools/generate_state_machine_types.py), the discriminated unions, the initial values, the guard names and, compiled from each guard's condition, one judgment per guard (SD-3; the unit writes by hand only the named functions of `xGuardLanguage` a condition calls, under the same names). The transition-table constant is printed only where code reads it -- the unit itself or another file (JDG-139; the generator's TRANSITIONS_READ) -- today task-group-folding.ts alone (TREE_STATE_TRANSITIONS, table T-328); CR-573 removed the tests that were the only readers of the others. A region that holds documentData (SD-5) gets only its events, its guard names and judgments and, where it is read, its transition-table constant; each of its judgments takes one input -- the task group the cell decides (null in a root cell), the values the event carries and the named functions -- so the transition function looks a cell's guard up by name; and its state keys must be the enum values of the erd.json column it names, in the same order.
Rebuild: npm run gen   |   npm run gen:check fails if anything has drifted.

Validated by docs/development-rules/manuscript-schemas/state-machines.schema.json before a byte is written. state_machine_source.py and both generators also refuse: a key of the standard's levels that is neither the standard's nor starts with `x`, a pair of a leaf state and an event answered twice or not at all, an `initial` that is not the initial transition's source, an evidence id docs/spec does not define, a transition whose source or target is not a state of its machine, an event a table uses that its region does not define, a union without exactly one initial state (none in a composite entered only by naming a child), a machine name or event key used twice, a machine name that does not end in StateMachine, a guard a transition names that its region does not define (or one defined but never named), and a condition the guard language cannot read or whose terms do not resolve.

Guard conditions are here (each region's `guards`, in the language of `xGuardLanguage`), and the code's judgments are generated from them; effect bodies and the bodies of the named functions are NOT -- the code holds them (SD-3). Every string that is printed prose is a language dictionary.

PRIORITIES ARE ONE TABLE ACROSS THE REGIONS (SD-4, table T-283): per contested key, its rungs in the order they consume it, each naming the states that stand on it with ids this file already defines. The ORDER is not this file's: it is the requirement rows each rung cites (IN-4, SK-19, NT-7), and the generator holds the Esc rungs word for word, in order, against the chain IN-4 writes with arrows. Printed at the head of _assets/tbl-state-machines.md; no code constant is generated from it -- the code's Esc rung is escapeTarget.
